description:
We are a team of three enthusiastic Form 2 students from Sarawak, Malaysia, who share a passion for STEM, technology, and space exploration. We enjoy programming, creative problem-solving, and exploring innovative solutions to real-world challenges.

Through the Sarawak Space Challenge, we aim to enhance our creativity, teamwork, and technical skills while gaining valuable experience and turning our ideas into practical solutions.

Orvital is an astronaut health monitoring and support application developed by Team AstraVita to address the unique health challenges of space missions.

Astronauts face risks such as muscle and bone loss, sleep disturbances, psychological stress, vision changes, and environmental hazards. Orvital aims to help astronauts track their health and respond to potential concerns through a simple, accessible mobile interface.

The app is designed to combine daily health check-ins, medical and environmental measurements, health trend analysis, and personalized countermeasures. Additional planned features include reminders, test result storage, and an Emergency section with AI-assisted guidance and SOS contact options.

By integrating health monitoring, evaluation, and practical support, Orvital aims to transform health data into meaningful insights and actionable recommendations, helping astronauts manage their well-being throughout space missions.
details:
1. Project Overview

Orvital is an astronaut health monitoring and support application developed by Team AstraVita, a team of three Form 2 students from Sarawak, Malaysia.

Astronauts face unique health challenges during space missions, including muscle and bone loss, sleep disturbances, psychological stress, vision changes, cardiovascular changes, and exposure to environmental hazards such as radiation and elevated carbon dioxide levels.

Our project aims to address these challenges by providing a user-friendly mobile application that helps astronauts monitor their health, identify potential concerns, and access practical health guidance. Rather than simply displaying health measurements, Orvital focuses on connecting health monitoring, evaluation, and appropriate actions within a single platform.

2. How Orvital Works

Orvital is designed around five main sections: Home, Health Log, Insights, Care, and Emergency.

The Home Dashboard provides astronauts with a concise overview of their health status. It includes Today's Health Brief, Today's Plan with daily check-in progress, and Quick Values displaying recent health information. Astronauts can also access their profiles and mission settings.

The Health Log allows users to record daily health information through six categories: Space Adaptation, Exercise and Recovery, Vision, Stress and Mood, Sleep, and Nutrition and Hydration. Each category provides relevant input options while allowing users to describe additional symptoms or observations. This helps make health recording both organized and flexible.

The application also supports the recording of medical and environmental measurements, including heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature, cabin CO₂ levels, and radiation readings. These measurements are intended to be entered using information obtained from appropriate instruments, rather than being automatically measured by the smartphone.

The Insights section is designed to evaluate recorded health information, display trends, and highlight patterns that may require attention. For example, repeated sleep disturbances or reported vision changes can be identified through health records, helping users recognize potential concerns.

The Care section focuses on practical support. It provides health recommendations, astronaut-specific countermeasures, and activities related to exercise, sleep, stress management, and other health challenges associated with space missions. These features aim to encourage users to take appropriate action based on their recorded health information.

The Emergency section is designed to combine SOS contact functionality with an AI-assisted chat. Users can describe their symptoms or concerns freely and receive general guidance to help them understand the situation and communicate relevant information. The SOS function provides a separate way to contact designated emergency personnel without depending on an AI response.

Additional features include customizable reminders, mission settings, health-related achievements, and medical test result storage. The Test Results feature is designed to support PDF and image files, with an optional AI-assisted explanation function to help users understand uploaded medical information.

3. Innovation and Benefits

Orvital aims to go beyond conventional health tracking by integrating three essential processes: monitoring, evaluation, and action.

Instead of requiring astronauts to interpret isolated measurements independently, the application is designed to organize their health records, identify potentially concerning patterns, and connect users with relevant health guidance and countermeasures.

One of the key aspects of our project is its focus on astronaut-specific health challenges. By considering the effects of microgravity, isolation, altered environments, and other space-related conditions, Orvital aims to provide a monitoring experience that is more relevant to space missions than a general fitness application.

We also prioritize accessibility and ease of use. The application uses a clean interface, clearly organized health categories, and flexible input methods to reduce unnecessary complexity while maintaining useful monitoring capabilities.

Our goal is to make health information easier to understand and turn recorded data into meaningful insights and practical recommendations.

4. Tools and Technologies

During the initial development stage, our team used Kodular, a visual block-based programming platform, to prototype and test essential functions such as user authentication, AI integration, and reminder notifications.

As our project progressed, we recognized the need for greater flexibility in interface design, customization, and feature integration. Therefore, we transitioned to HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to develop a more refined and interactive version of Orvital.

We then used the Android SDK (Software Development Kit) to build and package our application into an Android APK, allowing it to run on Android devices.

We also explored Firebase for user authentication and data management, alongside Google Gemini AI, connected through a JavaScript-based Cloudflare Worker, for AI-assisted functionality.

During prototyping, we successfully tested Firebase authentication, AI-generated responses, and notification functionality in an Android application. These experiments helped guide the development and integration of features in our newer version.

This development process reflects our team's adaptability, problem-solving skills, and commitment to continuous improvement by selecting technologies that best meet our project's requirements.

5. Considerations, Challenges, and Intended Impact

Throughout the development process, our team considered several important factors, including usability, data accuracy, privacy, technical feasibility, and the unique health risks associated with space exploration.

One of our challenges was developing a mobile application that could offer meaningful health support without relying on specialized medical sensors built into the smartphone. To address this, we designed a system that allows users to record measurements obtained from appropriate instruments and combine them with daily observations.

Another challenge involved balancing functionality with simplicity. We aimed to provide useful features without overwhelming users with excessive information or complicated input procedures.

We also considered the limitations of AI-assisted health guidance. Orvital is intended to support health awareness, monitoring, and communication rather than replace professional medical assessment or mission medical personnel. AI-generated responses should be treated as supplementary information, particularly in emergency situations.

Our long-term vision is to contribute to more proactive and accessible astronaut health management. By connecting daily monitoring, health evaluation, and practical support, Orvital aims to help astronauts recognize potential concerns, better understand their health conditions, and take appropriate steps throughout their missions.

Through this project, Team AstraVita hopes to demonstrate how creativity, accessible technology, and collaborative problem-solving can contribute to addressing real-world challenges in space exploration.
